reason: The bone-lineage environment should direct the stem-cell descendants toward the cells needed for living bone.

reaction: The distinction between matrix-producing osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes is useful.
reason: Mineralizing the collagen framework is a plausible next step toward strong arm bones.

reaction: The contrast between collagen's toughness and mineral's resistance to compression is useful.
reason: Adding the bone cells to the mineralised framework should help make it living bone.
expectation: The bone cells will become part of the arm-bone structure.

reaction: The automatic compatibility feedback clarified the order.

choice.combine: Bone cells linked to a blood supply

expectation: The supplied cells will join the framework to form living arm bones.

effect: The supplied cells and mineralised framework formed living arm bones, completing the bone goal and revealing a joint-connection goal.
reaction: The cutaway makes the route from blood vessels to embedded bone cells clearer.
reason: The synovial membrane is described as a lining, and the fibrous sleeve has an unlined inner face.
expectation: The membrane will line the sleeve to form a joint capsule.

effect: The synovial membrane lined the fibrous sleeve, completing the capsule goal; the bones still need to be connected into a movable joint.
reaction: The lining's contribution to joint fluid makes its role clearer.
reason: The smooth cartilage caps should cover the living bone ends where they meet at the joint.
expectation: The cartilage will be added to the joint surfaces of the arm bones.

effect: The cartilage now covers the facing elbow surfaces, preparing the bones to slide against one another.
reaction: The sliding inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: The lined capsule surrounds the joint cavity, so combining it with the cartilage-covered bones is a plausible next step toward the joint.
expectation: The capsule will surround the cartilage-covered bone ends to form a joint.

alternatives.reason: The ligaments might need to connect the bones before the capsule is added.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with fluid helping the surfaces glide.
reaction: The cutaway clarifies how the lining and cartilage work together.
reason: The remaining ligaments span the elbow and should provide the restraint needed for a supported joint.
expectation: The ligaments will reinforce the elbow while allowing movement.

effect: The ligaments completed the supported, movable elbow, showing bending alongside resistance to sideways movement; all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The contrasting movement arrows make the ligaments’ restraining role clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the joint from cartilage, capsule and ligaments was most worthwhile: the planned cutaways connect each structure to gliding, enclosure or restraint.

leastWorthwhile.text: The two successive bone-supply cutaways repeated much of the same vessel-to-cell nutrient route, making the second less informative.

surprise.text: I expected to add bone cells directly to the mineralised framework, but compatibility feedback first linked them to blood vessels. The planned picture distinguished nutrient-filled channels from the vessel containing red blood cells.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the cells and vessels to be combined before adding them to the framework felt like a construction-order constraint rather than an obvious biological necessity, although the resulting supply route had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: assembling the joint made the relationship between structure and movement concrete, and I would be curious to see how muscles move it.
